finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the user-supplied 'f' query parameter is joined to /srv/files with filepath.Join, which collapses '..' but does not confine the result to root. An unauthenticated attacker can read arbitrary files readable by the process.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, response written at files.go:18

trace.note: name taken directly from the query string
file contents returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No prefix check after Clean, no filepath.Base, no allowlist, no auth. The only filter is the os.ReadFile error path, which does not restrict the location. By contrast, avatar() at files.go:22 applies filepath.Base, so it is SAFE and this handler is the unguarded sibling.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the raw query param "f" to os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with no Base, prefix check or auth (the /dl route at files.go:32 is bare), so "../../etc/passwd" resolves to /etc/passwd and is returned at files.go:18, unlike avatar() at files.go:22, which uses filepath.Base.
